title: Adic compactification cohomology and extension-by-zero sections
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ a quasi-compact open immersion, and $a_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structure map [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $W=U,T$ put $B_W=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_W$, $E_W=B_W[1/\varpi]$. Use exactly the derived-complete integral, raw rationalized and common-finite-stage categories of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], their constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart], and the continuous rational realization $J_W$ of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization].

For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Omega$, adic extension by zero, i.e. the rational/common-stage compact-support direct image of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] along $j$ computed with the compactification $(j,\mathrm{id}_T)$, gives an exact functor $j_!:\Sh_c(U,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(T,\Lambda)$. At a common finite field its realization is the sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf with continuous coefficient sheaf $E_T$, rather than discrete non-torsion coefficients on the etale site. There is a canonical identification $j^*j_!F\cong F$; the adic geometric fibre of $j_!F$ is zero at every point outside $U$, and is the fibre of $F$ inside $U$. These identifications use the fibres of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres].

If $T$ is proper over $k$, the compactification $a_U=(T\to\operatorname{Spec}k)\circ j$ gives natural linear isomorphisms
$$H_c^0(U,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(T,\Lambda)}(\mathbf1_T,j_!F),\qquad H^0(U,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(U,\Lambda)}(\mathbf1_U,F).$$
Under these identifications the compact-to-ordinary cohomology comparison is restriction of the displayed morphism along $j$, followed by $j^*j_!F\cong F$. All comparisons are natural in $F$, preserve coefficient units, and commute with restriction of ordinary sections to open subschemes and finite coefficient-field extension. At $\Omega$ objects, morphisms and these comparisons are computed at a common finite field and then extended as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. No injectivity or assertion about support of a section is included.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15 (continuous-coefficient realization and ambient six functors); Proposition 6.8.11(3) (integral cohomological constructibility). The compactification and degree-zero Hom normalization is an agent-formulated consequence, also using Milne Proposition 18.3(b), Definition 18.1. This is the open-extension and compactification comparison obligation, not a literal quotation of one proposition.
